---
title: "How do I measure a monotonic relationship when linear correlation is unsuitable?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I measure a monotonic relationship when linear correlation is unsuitable?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Check observations are paired and have a meaningful order.

2. Plot them.

3. Use cor.test(x,y,method='spearman') and interpret the rank association.

## Runnable example

```{r}
x <- c(1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8)
y <- c(1,4,9,16,25,36,49,64)
print(c(pearson=cor(x,y,method="pearson"),
        spearman=cor(x,y,method="spearman")))
print(cor.test(x,y,method="spearman")$estimate)
```

## Interpret the result

The relationship is increasing but curved. Spearman's rho is 1 because the ranks increase in exactly the same order, even though the Pearson coefficient is not 1.

## Check before using real data

Spearman correlation does not measure every kind of nonlinear pattern, and tied ranks affect exact p-value calculations.
